feature.text: Olympics, FIFA World Cups, UEFA, the NFL and Formula 1, from the first web team at Deltatre in 1995 to Chief Product & Marketing Officer and Group Chief Evangelist. scarf.title: Why the scarf
scarf.text: The scarf came first. For years I turned up at conferences in big scarves, the kind you notice from the back of the room, and people started remembering the scarf before the surname. The name stuck the day David Cushnan introduced me from the stage at Leaders Week in London as a guy with a scarf. The newsletter followed on 15 November 2022, and the title was never in doubt.

stage_page.title: On stage, online and on air
stage_page.intro: Moderation is preparation. Before a panel I read what each guest has published in the last year, write the questions they have not been asked, and cut the ones they have. On the day the job is to keep the clock, stop the pitch, and let the disagreement happen. Keynotes get the same treatment in reverse: one argument, the numbers that carry it, and the slide count kept low enough that people look at me.
stage_page.offer: Available as moderator, host or keynote speaker for conferences, client events, webinars and podcasts, in English and Italian, remote or in person. Turin is the base; London, Madrid, Düsseldorf and Monaco were the stages of the last twelve months.

brand.title: Brand guidelines
brand.intro: One person, one name, one mark. This page is for anyone who puts them on something: a conference slide, a partner page, a post, a credit line. It says what the mark is, which colours it uses, how the name is written, and what not to do. Everything on it can be downloaded below.
brand.mark_p1: Four horizontal bars, solid at the left, breaking into particles toward the right. Read left to right it is a broadcast becoming data: a match, a feed, a season turned into the points a chart or a model works with. That is the work, sports media, digital and AI, in one gesture.
brand.mark_p2: The four colours come from the scarf in the photo on the home page. The scarf is an accident that stuck; the mark is not about it. The bars always run left to right, always in this order from the top: sand, turquoise, cobalt, red.
brand.versions_p: Four files cover every use. The tile is for browser tabs, app icons and avatars. The wide mark sits next to the name in a masthead or a credit line. The bare mark is the tile without its background, for a page that already has a dark or white ground. The stacked lockup puts the mark over the name, for squares, posts and slides.

versions.name: Tile
versions.use: Favicon, app icon, avatar. Ink background, 7 px corner on 32. Works on light and dark tab bars.

versions.name: Tile, paper
versions.use: The same on white, for places that want a light tile.

versions.name: Wide mark
versions.use: Next to the name at 20 to 28 px tall, or large on its own. The particles have room to dissolve.

versions.name: Stacked lockup
versions.use: Mark over the name, name set as outlines. For a square, a post, a slide. Dark and with-person versions below.

versions.name: Bare mark
versions.use: No tile. On white or on a dark ground, never on a photograph or a colour.

versions.name: Touch icon
versions.use: Square, no rounding: iOS rounds it. Export to 180 px PNG.

size_items: 16 px. The bars still read; the particles become a frayed edge, which is fine.
20 px tall. Below that, use the tile.
One bar height on every side. Nothing else sits inside it.
Mark first, then the name, on one baseline, a gap of half the mark's height.
Side by side in mastheads and credit lines. Stacked where the space is square or the name must be large: posts, slides, the end of a video.
brand.colour_p: The four colours belong to the mark and to data. Text is ink on paper, or paper on night in the apps. Cobalt is the only one of the four that holds as a link colour on both grounds; the other three never carry text.

colours.name: Paper
colours.role: Ground of the root site and the light hubs

brand.name_p1: A Guy With A Scarf. Title case, every word, always complete. In a byline or a masthead it is followed by the person: A Guy With A Scarf · Carlo De Marchis, with the name in mute.
brand.name_p2: AGWAS is a file name and a way of talking, not a public mark. Never "a guy with a scarf" in lower case, never "Guy with a Scarf", never "AGWAS" in a title.
brand.type_p: Helvetica Neue, with Helvetica and Arial as fallbacks. The name is set in weight 500. Headings are 300 or 400 with tight letter spacing; body text is 400. The sport apps keep their own faces inside; the name and the mark look the same everywhere.
donts: Mirror the mark or run the particles right to left.
Recolour the bars, drop one, or reorder them.
Stretch the tile or the wide mark; scale them as a block.
Put the bare mark on a photograph, a gradient or a colour.
Add a scarf, a letter or a sport pictogram to it.
Set the name in lower case, in a serif, or as an acronym.
brand.download_p: SVG, which scales to any size. Export PNG from the SVG when a format needs it.
